title: RiverScan: Learning to Accumulate on River Networks
abstract: arXiv:2611.18005v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Accurate runoff prediction across large river basins requires models to capture heterogeneous local hydrological responses and their accumulation downstream. River-network connectivity provides a natural structure for this task, but using it effectively requires learning how to combine contributions from subcatchments of different sizes. We frame this challenge as learning to accumulate and introduce RiverScan, a spatial operator based on area-weighted selective state-space recurrence. RiverScan recursively combines local temporal representations with accumulated upstream states in topological order. Contributing-area fractions account for subcatchment size, while learned retention controls how upstream information persists downstream. Experiments on 608 stations in the Danube basin show that RiverScan outperforms the evaluated temporal and graph baselines in overall predictive performance. translated_title: RiverScan：学习在河网上进行累积
translated_abstract: 准确的大流域径流预测要求模型能够捕捉异质性的局地水文响应及其向下游的累积过程。河网连通性为这一任务提供了天然的结构，但要有效利用它，需要学习如何合并来自不同尺度子流域的贡献。我们将这一挑战表述为“学习累积”，并提出 RiverScan——一种基于面积加权选择性状态空间递归的空间算子。RiverScan 按拓扑顺序递归地将局地时间表示与上游累积状态相结合。汇流面积比例用于刻画子流域的大小，而可学习的持留机制则控制上游信息向下游的持续传递。在多瑙河流域 608 个站点的实验表明，RiverScan 在整体预测性能上优于所评估的时序模型与图基线方法。结构性控制实验与消融研究证明了……
tldr: 提出 RiverScan——一种基于面积加权选择性状态空间递归的空间算子，按拓扑顺序学习河网上的信息累积，在多瑙河流域 608 个站点的径流预测中超越了时序与图基线方法。
en_tdlr: RiverScan, a spatial operator based on area-weighted selective state-space recurrence, learns to accumulate upstream contributions along river networks, outperforming temporal and graph baselines for runoff prediction across 608 stations in the Danube basin.
